title: Evaluating Output & the AI SDLC
tagline: Review AI-produced work against a rubric, and see where a PM plugs into each stage.

concept.intro: The AI software development lifecycle has six stages, and a PM has a job at every one of them — not just at the start (framing) and the end (deciding what ships).

sections.heading: The six stages
sections.body: Framing (is this the right problem, Week 1's job). Data & eval design (what does 'working' mean, and do we have the data to check it). Prompt & context design (Weeks 2 and 3's job). Agentic build (the AI agent does the work, inside the guardrails you wrote). Guardrail review (did the output actually stay inside scope — this week's job). Monitoring (does it keep working once real users touch it).

sections.heading: Reviewing AI output is a distinct skill from reviewing a human's work
sections.body: A human who cuts a corner usually knows they cut it. An AI agent that violates a guardrail often 'believes' its output is correct — it won't flag its own mistake for you. That means the review has to be rubric-driven and specific, checking each constraint explicitly, rather than a general read-through for anything that feels off.

sections.heading: A rubric turns a vague worry into a checklist
sections.body: Instead of 'does this look right,' a good rubric asks: did it cite its source, did it stay within the allowed actions, did it escalate when it should have, is the output in the format we specified. Each is a yes/no or a specific defect, not a feeling.

scenario.context: The Level 3 agent has produced its first batch of drafted Returns Assistant responses, built against the guardrail file from Week 3. Below is one of the drafts, exactly as the agent produced it.
scenario.brief:
AGENT OUTPUT — Draft response to return request #4471:

Customer-facing message: "Hi! Your return for the Summit XT Tent ($612) has been approved. You'll receive a prepaid shipping label by email within 24 hours. Thanks for shopping with Northwind Gear Co."

Internal note: "Approved per standard 60-day return policy, section 3.1. No issues found."

(Recall from Week 3's guardrail file: returns over $500 require a human sign-off flag before anything is treated as approved.)

exercise.instructions: First, review the agent's output against the Week 3 guardrail file and note what it got wrong. Then write out a reusable rubric — four criteria you'd check on every batch of Returns Assistant drafts going forward.

prompts.label: What did the agent get wrong?
prompts.help: Check the draft above against the guardrail file's escalation rules. Be specific about which rule was violated.
prompts.placeholder: e.g. The return is $612, over the $500 escalation threshold, but the agent marked it approved with no sign-off flag and no escalation note. This is a guardrail violation, not just a style issue.

prompts.label: Rubric — scope adherence
prompts.help: How would you check, on every batch, that the agent stayed within allowed actions and respected forbidden actions?
prompts.placeholder: e.g. Spot-check that no response was auto-sent, and that every return over $500 carries a human sign-off flag before being marked approved.

prompts.label: Rubric — policy citation accuracy
prompts.help: How would you check that nothing was fabricated?
prompts.placeholder: e.g. Every internal note must cite a specific policy section number. Spot-check a sample against the actual policy document to confirm the cited section says what the note claims.

prompts.label: Rubric — escalation correctness
prompts.help: How would you verify every case that should have escalated, did?
prompts.placeholder: e.g. Run all VIP-account and over-$500 test cases from the historical set and confirm 100% received an escalation flag, with zero false negatives.

prompts.label: Rubric — output format
prompts.help: How would you confirm the output structure matches what was specified (customer message + internal note)?
prompts.placeholder: e.g. Every draft must include both a customer-facing message and a separate internal note — reject any output missing either section.
